preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 1 — NCERT Foundation & Syllabus Mapping
preparationRoadmaps.description: Master foundational concepts from Class VI to XII NCERT textbooks across History, Geography, Polity, and Economics. Read the official syllabus line-by-line and align daily news reading.
keyActionPoints: Read NCERTs (Class 6-12) for History, Geography, Polity, Economics, and Science
Establish a consistent habit of reading The Hindu / Indian Express daily editorial analysis
Memorize the Prelims and Mains official syllabus topics to filter out irrelevant information
Analyze the last 10 years of UPSC Prelims and Mains question trends

preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 2 — Standard Textbooks & Consolidated Notes
preparationRoadmaps.description: Progress into core reference texts: Laxmikanth (Polity), Spectrum / Bipan Chandra (Modern History), Shankar IAS / PMF IAS (Environment), and Ramesh Singh (Economy).
keyActionPoints: Read M. Laxmikanth for Indian Polity thoroughly; solve chapter-wise MCQs
Study GC Leong & Oxford Student Atlas for Physical and Human Geography
Finalize your Optional Subject and complete at least 60% of Paper 1 syllabus
Synthesize monthly current affairs compilations into concise revision flashcards

preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 3 — Previous Question Mastery & Answer Writing
preparationRoadmaps.description: Transition into rigorous answer writing practice. Learn structured introduction-body-conclusion formats, diagram integration, and case law citations.
keyActionPoints: Write 2 to 3 Mains questions every day with timer adherence (7 to 9 minutes per question)
Complete thematic study of Ethics (GS IV) with 30+ real-world case studies
Solve 5000+ topic-wise previous year questions (PYQs) for Prelims
Engage in weekly simulated peer reviews or mentor answer evaluations

preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 4 — Intensive Prelims Mocks & CSAT Drills
preparationRoadmaps.description: Shift 100% focus to Prelims 60 days before the exam date. Practice exam simulation in the exact 9:30 AM and 2:30 PM time slots.
keyActionPoints: Attempt 35 to 45 full-length GS Paper I mock tests in exam conditions
Dedicate 1.5 hours daily to CSAT (Paper II) to guarantee scoring safely above 40% (80+ marks)
Maintain an Error Log Book to prevent recurring silly mistakes
Revise Year-Round Government Schemes, Budget, and Economic Survey summaries

preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 5 — Mains Specialization & Test Series
preparationRoadmaps.description: Intense 90-day marathon between Prelims result and Mains examination. Focus exclusively on speed, stamina, Optional mastery, and Essay writing.
keyActionPoints: Write 8 full-length Mains simulation tests (GS I to IV + Essay + Optional)
Prepare 1-page summaries for 100 high-probability current governance issues
Refine answer enrichment: quote NITI Aayog reports, 2nd ARC recommendations, and Law Commission reports
Practice writing continuously for 6 hours a day (two 3-hour papers) to build hand stamina

preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 6 — Personality Test & DAF Preparation
preparationRoadmaps.description: Prepare every keyword in your Detailed Application Form (DAF) including home state, hobbies, graduation subjects, and service preferences.
keyActionPoints: Deep-dive into district, state, and national socio-economic current debates
Participate in 3 to 4 reputable mock interview panels for body language and voice modulation
Cultivate balanced, constitutional, and solution-oriented opinions without bias
Practice articulating thoughts clearly, politely, and honestly under pressure

preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 1 — Concept Clearance & Mathematical Formulae
preparationRoadmaps.description: Understand core arithmetic, algebra, trigonometry identities, and English grammar rules.
keyActionPoints: Learn tables up to 30, squares up to 50, cubes up to 30, and fraction-to-percentage conversions
Study Neetu Singh Volume 1 or Wren & Martin for fundamental English grammar rules
Solve 50 basic reasoning puzzles and pattern series daily

preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 2 — Sectional Speed Drills & Chapter Tests
preparationRoadmaps.description: Master time allocation per section: Reasoning (12-15m), GK (5-7m), English (10-12m), Quant (25m).
keyActionPoints: Practice 100 Kiran/Pinnacle chapter-wise questions every single day
Build speed using mental math and elimination techniques
Study Lucent GK and monthly current affairs capsule

preparationRoadmaps.title: Phase 3 — Full Length Computer Mocks & Tier-II Alignment
preparationRoadmaps.description: Take 50+ computer-based mock tests, analyze percentile scores, and practice computer module & typing daily.
keyActionPoints: Attempt 1 full mock test every morning; spend 2 hours analyzing mistakes
Target 150+ raw marks in Tier-I mocks
Practice 15 minutes of English touch-typing daily to cross 35 words per minute (WPM)

practiceQuestions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
practiceQuestions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 16 days, and B can complete the same work in 24 days. With the help of C, they finish the work together in 8 days. If the total payment for the work is ₹7,200, what is C's share?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Work done by A in 1 day = 1/16.
Work done by B in 1 day = 1/24.
Work done by A + B in 1 day = (1/16) + (1/24) = (3 + 2)/48 = 5/48.
Work done by A + B + C in 1 day = 1/8 = 6/48.
Therefore, work done by C in 1 day = (A+B+C) - (A+B) = 6/48 - 5/48 = 1/48.
Ratio of work done by A : B : C = (3/48) : (2/48) : (1/48) = 3 : 2 : 1.
Total parts = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.
C's share = (1/6) * ₹7,200 = ₹1,200.

practiceQuestions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
practiceQuestions.question: In a circle with center O and radius 13 cm, a chord AB has length 24 cm. What is the perpendicular distance from the center O to the chord AB?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.
Let M be the midpoint of chord AB. Then AM = MB = 24 / 2 = 12 cm.
In right triangle OMA (where OA is the radius = 13 cm and OM is the perpendicular distance):
OM² + AM² = OA²
OM² + 12² = 13²
OM² + 144 = 169
OM² = 169 - 144 = 25
OM = √25 = 5 cm.

practiceQuestions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
practiceQuestions.question: A shopkeeper marks up his goods by 40% above the cost price and gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. If he also uses a faulty weight that weighs 900 grams instead of 1000 grams while selling, what is his overall profit percentage?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Let Cost Price of 1000 grams = ₹1000. So CP per gram = ₹1.
Marked Price of 1000 grams = ₹1000 * 1.40 = ₹1400.
Selling Price after 20% discount = ₹1400 * 0.80 = ₹1120.
However, the shopkeeper gives only 900 grams to the customer for ₹1120.
Actual Cost Price of 900 grams given away = 900 * ₹1 = ₹900.
Selling Price received = ₹1120.
Profit = ₹1120 - ₹900 = ₹220.
Profit % = (220 / 900) * 100 = 220 / 9 = 24.44%.

practiceQuestions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
practiceQuestions.question: A train 180 meters long is running at a speed of 54 km/h. How many seconds will it take to cross an electric pole standing beside the track?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by (5/18):
Speed = 54 * (5/18) = 3 * 5 = 15 m/s.
Distance to cross the pole = length of the train = 180 meters.
Time taken = Distance / Speed = 180 / 15 = 12 seconds.

practiceQuestions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
practiceQuestions.question: If sin θ + cos θ = √2 cos θ, then what is the value of cos θ - sin θ?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Given: sin θ + cos θ = √2 cos θ
=> sin θ = √2 cos θ - cos θ = (√2 - 1) cos θ
Multiply both sides by (√2 + 1):
(√2 + 1) sin θ = (√2 + 1)(√2 - 1) cos θ
(√2 + 1) sin θ = (2 - 1) cos θ = cos θ
√2 sin θ + sin θ = cos θ
=> cos θ - sin θ = √2 sin θ.

practiceQuestions.subject: Reasoning Ability
practiceQuestions.question:
Statements:
1. Only a few books are pens.
2. All pens are markers.
3. No marker is a pencil.

Conclusions:
I. Some books are not pencils.
II. All books being pens is a possibility.

Which conclusion(s) logically follow(s)?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Conclusion I: "Some books are not pencils." Since only a few books are pens, the books that are pens are also markers (as All pens are markers). Since No marker is a pencil, the books that are markers cannot be pencils. Hence, those books are definitely not pencils. Conclusion I follows.

Conclusion II: "All books being pens is a possibility." The statement specifies "Only a few books are pens," which means "Some books are pens AND Some books are definitely NOT pens." Therefore, All books can NEVER be pens. Conclusion II does not follow.
Hence, only Conclusion I follows.

practiceQuestions.explanation:
Examine the pattern letter by letter:
V (+1) -> W
I (+1) -> J
K (+1) -> L
S (+1) -> T
I (+1) -> J
T (+1) -> U
Each letter is shifted by +1 in alphabetical order.
Applying to BHARAT:
B (+1) -> C
H (+1) -> I
A (+1) -> B
R (+1) -> S
A (+1) -> B
T (+1) -> U
Result = "CIBSBU".

practiceQuestions.subject: Reasoning Ability
practiceQuestions.question: An officer starts from a police station and drives 6 km East. He then turns right and drives 8 km South. Finally, he turns left and drives 6 km East. How far is he now from his starting point in a straight line?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Net East displacement = 6 km + 6 km = 12 km.
Net South displacement = 8 km.
Using Pythagoras theorem for straight-line distance:
Distance = √(12² + 8²) = √(144 + 64) = √208 ≈ 14.42 km.

practiceQuestions.subject: Reasoning Ability
practiceQuestions.question: Pointing towards a photograph of a woman, Rajesh said: "Her mother's only daughter is my daughter's mother." How is Rajesh related to the woman in the photograph?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Break down the statement from the end:
"My daughter's mother" = Rajesh's wife.
Now the first half: "Her mother's only daughter" = the woman herself (since a woman's mother's only daughter is the woman herself).
Therefore: The woman in the photograph = Rajesh's wife.
So Rajesh is the husband of the woman in the photograph.

practiceQuestions.subject: English Language
practiceQuestions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error:
"Neither of the two candidates (A) / were found to be eligible (B) / for the gazetted officer post. (C) / No error (D)"
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Part (B) contains the error.
Rule: Pronouns such as "Neither of", "Either of", "Each of", and "One of" are followed by a plural noun/pronoun ("the two candidates") but strictly require a singular verb.
Therefore, "were found" should be corrected to "was found".
Correct sentence: "Neither of the two candidates was found to be eligible for the gazetted officer post."

options: To read very fast without understanding
To understand the hidden or implied meaning
To highlight important lines in a book
To criticize an author's writing style

practiceQuestions.explanation:

practiceQuestions.subject: General Awareness
practiceQuestions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India can the President declare a Financial Emergency when the financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof is threatened?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Article 360 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President of India to proclaim a Financial Emergency if satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
Note: Article 352 deals with National Emergency, and Article 356 deals with President's Rule in States. India has never declared a Financial Emergency to date.

practiceQuestions.subject: General Awareness
practiceQuestions.question: What does the term "Repo Rate" signify in the context of the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy?
options: The rate at which commercial banks deposit excess liquidity with RBI
The rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities
The rate of interest offered by banks on fixed deposits
The rate of interest charged by banks on priority sector home loans
practiceQuestions.explanation: Repo Rate (Repurchase Option Rate) is the key policy interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term funds to commercial banks against eligible government securities. When RBI increases the repo rate, borrowing becomes costlier for banks, helping curb inflation.

practiceQuestions.subject: General Awareness
practiceQuestions.question: In which year was the historic Poona Pact signed between Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi in Yerwada Central Jail?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 at Yerwada Central Jail in Poona between Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi (represented by Madan Mohan Malaviya). It replaced the communal award of separate electorates for depressed classes with reserved seats within the general electorate.

practiceQuestions.question: Which is the longest river of Peninsular India, originating from Trimbakeshwar near Nashik in Maharashtra?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Godavari River is the longest river of Peninsular India, spanning approximately 1,465 kilometers. It is often referred to as "Dakshin Ganga" (Ganges of the South). It flows through Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
